45137.title: Purchase Orders rank by Ordered status and recency
45137.preconds: 1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip. 2. Have several purchase orders matching one term: at least one still 'Ordered' (not yet received) and at least one 'Received'; some created recently and some created weeks ago; and at least one created by the signed-in user versus one created by someone else.
45137.steps: 1. Type the term that matches the seeded purchase orders (use the 'Purchase Orders' tab if it helps to focus on them). 2. Read the order of the PO rows. 3. Confirm an Ordered (not yet received) PO ranks above a Received one. 4. Confirm a more recently created PO ranks above an older one. 5. Confirm a PO created by you gets a small extra boost over an otherwise-equal PO created by someone else.
45137.expected: Expected results A Purchase Order still Ordered (not yet received) ranks above received ones. More recently created POs rank above older ones (recency fades over about two weeks). A PO created by the signed-in user gets a small extra lift. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-9160; Global Search — Product Requirements, Confluence page 576978945, version 1.5 (read 22 September 2026), §6.1. Last checked against build v26.36.7-29ca209 on 9/17/2026. Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) §6.1: “Status = Ordered (not yet received) → +0.30; recency of creation, exponential decay with 14-day half-life, up to +0.25; created-by = current user → +0.10.” AUTOMATION: READY

53476.title: No count in the search modal reads higher than 20
53476.refs: SV-9160 (PRD 5.2 counts capped at 20; 2 no pagination)
53476.preconds: 1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press the keyboard shortcut) to open the global search. 2. Test data exists so that at least one entity type has more than 20 matches for a short query (for example many Work Orders).
53476.steps: 1. Type a short term that matches more than 20 records of one entity type (for example a common Work Order fragment). 2. Read the entity's scope tab count, its group heading count, and the 'Show all N' link. 3. Click that entity's scope tab and count the rows shown.
53476.expected: 1. No count anywhere in the modal reads higher than 20 - not the scope tab (for example 'Work Orders (20)'), not the group heading, and not the 'Show all N' link ('Show all 20'). 2. A query matching 34 Work Orders shows 'Work Orders (20)' and 'Show all 20', never the true 34. 3. The scoped tab shows at most 20 rows, scrolled inside the modal, with no pagination and no further loading. This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 2 (Non-Goals: no pagination) and section 5.2 (counts capped at 20), read on 16 September 2026. Last checked against build v26.36.7-21b4db9 on 9/16/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

55716.title: When two results are otherwise equal, the most recently updated one ranks first
55716.preconds: 1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip. 2. Seed two records of the same entity type that match one query equally well (same kind of match, and neither has any ranking advantage over the other) EXCEPT that one was updated more recently than the other.
55716.steps: 1. Type the shared query. 2. Read the order of the two rows within the group.
55716.expected: Expected results When everything else is equal, the more recently updated record ranks first. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-9160; Global Search — Product Requirements, Confluence page 576978945, version 1.5 (read 22 September 2026), §6.1. Last checked against build v26.36.7-29ca209 on 9/17/2026. Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) §6.1: “The score is clamped to a sane range; ties are broken by recency (most recently updated wins). Because search returns at most 20 records per entity type (§5.2), ranking quality is what decides whether the record the user wanted is reachable at all.” AUTOMATION: READY
